title: Renew a driver licence while temporarily interstate or overseas (using a photo-kit form)
summary: You can renew your NSW driver and/or rider licence either online or by completing and mailing a photo-kit form if you are temporarily interstate or overseas.
intro:

### Renew with a photo-kit form

You can complete a photo-kit form and send it by post to renew your licence if:

### Photo-kit renewal limits

There are limits that apply to renewing with the photo-kit form.

To renew your licence after you reach your limit you must visit a Service NSW Centre.

### If you are living interstate

Convert your NSW driver/rider licence to your current Australian state or territory if you are living there for 3 months or more continuously.

Under the national no-fee transfer system there is no fee to convert your current unrestricted or provisional licence from one state or territory to another. Your new licence will be issued with the remaining valid period if your NSW licence has not expired.

### If you are living overseas

If you have taken up residence in another country, apply for a driver/rider licence in that country.
who_can_apply: You are living interstate or overseas temporarily.

what_you_need: A colour passport size photograph as detailed on the form.
Your proof of identity as detailed on the form.
An appropriate witness as described on the form.
Accepted change of name document as listed on the form.
A change-of-name document that has been witnessed and certified if your proof of identity documents are in an old name due to a name change.
The completed photo-kit application form (downloadable PDF or by calling +61 2 8894 1599).

### Pay by post

If you are sending the form by post you can pay the fee by credit card: Mastercard, Visa or American Express.

Cash payments are not accepted by post.

faqs.q: How can I renew my NSW licence if I am temporarily interstate or overseas?
faqs.a: You can renew online, or you can complete a photo-kit form and send it by post.

faqs.q: What happens if I need to renew my licence after reaching the photo-kit limit?
faqs.a: You must visit a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: Do I need to change my licence if I am living interstate?
faqs.a: If you are living interstate for 3 months or more continuously, you can convert your NSW licence to your current state or territory. There is no fee under the national no-fee transfer system.
